sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: How bad is it, how fast is it growing, and what clocks are running?
criteria: Derives the eligibility error rate (2.3%) and compares it with other topics and last month to locate the failure
Estimates employees affected so far (about 1,739) and added harm per day (about 580), labelling the one-employee-per-conversation assumption
Names both clocks: 18 days left in the window and the day-48 late-add deadline
Puts containment ahead of root-cause analysis

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake, what does each want, and how do you bring them along?
criteria: Covers the escalating customer, all affected employers, employees, sales, legal and support, each with a distinct want
Addresses sales' request to notify only one customer and why it is declined
Reaches employees through their employers rather than directly
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What are the containment options, and how does each do on harm, contact-center load and speed?
criteria: Includes keep-running and full shutdown as options
Computes extra contacts for each option against the 2,500 of spare capacity
Shows that turning the topic off without cards overloads the center before the BPO arrives
Puts the options on one table with the same rows

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What do you do, what do you give up, and when would you restore generated answers?
criteria: Makes one call that combines rollback with narrow containment of the failing topic
Names what is given up, including handoffs for 30% of eligibility questions
Distinguishes reversible steps (flags, rollback) from the irreversible one (notification)
Sets a measurable condition for re-enabling generated eligibility answers

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What does each option cost over the rest of the window, and what revenue is at stake?
criteria: Prices overtime and BPO from the brief's per-contact costs for each option
Sizes the remediation review (about 302 hours) and who does it without cutting contact capacity
Puts the cost of keep-running in employees misled, not as zero
Weighs the response cost against the escalating customer's ARR and Q1 renewals, with the assumption labelled

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who runs the incident, and who owns each workstream?
criteria: Names one incident commander
Assigns separate owners for containment, remediation and customer notice
Gives the notification decision an executive owner
Keeps the postmortem blameless and owned by someone other than the release author

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What happens in the first hour, the first week and the next six weeks?
criteria: Contains within the first hour
Notifies all affected employers inside the 5-business-day contract window
Files carrier late-adds with slack before day 48
Has gates with checkable conditions, such as cards spot-checked or generation confirmed off in logs

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could still go wrong, and what stops the next release repeating this?
criteria: Re-checks every logged eligibility answer, not a sample, to find affected employees
Changes the release gate to judge each high-impact topic, not the overall average
Adds a runtime check of answers against the employer's plan rules
Avoids promising zero hallucinations

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How do you know the response worked, and what would it hide?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Tracks affected employees corrected, not just the error rate
Tracks handoff load against contact-center capacity
Ties at least one metric to renewals

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What does each audience hear, when, and from whom?
criteria: Gives a one-line message for at least four audiences, including affected employers and employees
Calls the escalating customer personally and early
Sets an update cadence that tightens during containment
Shares the postmortem with customers
